title: Can They Form an Arithmetic Progression?

concept.title: Compute the expected numbers and look them up
body: In an arithmetic progression of `n` numbers the smallest value is `lo`, the largest is `hi`, and the step is `d = (hi - lo) / (n - 1)`. If `hi - lo` is not divisible by `n - 1`, the step would not be a whole number. Otherwise the progression must be exactly `lo, lo + d, lo + 2d, ..., hi`. Put the given numbers in a set and check that every expected term is present, and that no number was repeated.

body.code:
present = set(a)
ok = len(present) == n and all(lo + i * d in present for i in range(n))

body: A special case: if all numbers are equal (`lo == hi`), the step is 0 and the answer is yes. This avoids sorting: finding the minimum and maximum and using a set takes O(n).

statement: Can the `n` numbers (`n >= 2`) be reordered to form an arithmetic progression, i.e. a sequence in which the difference between neighbours is always the same? Print `yes` or `no`.
hints: Find the smallest and the largest number.
The step must be `(hi - lo) / (n - 1)` and a whole number.
Check with a set that each of the terms `lo + i * d` is present, and that all numbers are different (unless the step is 0).

explanation: The smallest and largest number fix the step. A set confirms that every term of the progression is present exactly once.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

lo, hi = min(a), max(a)
if lo == hi:
    ok = True
elif (hi - lo) % (n - 1) != 0:
    ok = False
else:
    d = (hi - lo) // (n - 1)
    present = set(a)
    ok = len(present) == n and all(lo + i * d in present for i in range(n))
print("yes" if ok else "no")
